title: Split global app.css into route and component-owned style surfaces
description:
Problem: MemorySmith.App/wwwroot/app.css is now 3,726 lines and carries global styles for most route families. A selector-prefix scan found heavy concentrations for chat (164), wiki (98), admin (65), page/pages (92 combined), proposal/proposals (51 combined), tasks (36), maintenance (30), health (27), and about/profile/tag surfaces. This makes visual changes harder to review and increases the chance that one route's CSS fix changes another route.

Desired outcome: keep the current visual language while moving styles toward route/component-owned files or well-named shared primitives so UI changes have smaller review and regression surfaces.

Scope:
- In scope: inventory app.css sections, define shared primitives versus route-owned styles, introduce CSS isolation or grouped companion styles where compatible with Blazor/MudBlazor, and add style ownership notes for future UI tasks.
- Out of scope: broad redesign, palette changes, or behavior changes unrelated to style ownership.

Acceptance criteria:
- app.css is materially reduced or reorganized with clear route/component ownership boundaries.
- Shared primitives remain explicit and reusable rather than duplicated across route styles.
- Route smoke and visual/browser checks cover at least Memories, Pages, Chat, Admin, Tasks, Health, and About after extraction.
- Future UI tasks can identify the owning style surface without scanning the whole global stylesheet.

Validation:
- Run dotnet build MemorySmith.App/MemorySmith.App.csproj --nologo.
- Run route-smoke or equivalent browser checks for the affected routes.
- Run ./Scripts/Test-TaskRecords.ps1 after task metadata changes.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Created during 2026-05-25 deepdive audit. Evidence: clean source-only largest-file scan listed MemorySmith.App/wwwroot/app.css as the largest source file at 3,726 lines; selector-prefix scan found the highest class-prefix counts in chat, wiki, admin, page/pages, proposal/proposals, tasks, maintenance, health, about, profile, and tag surfaces. Existing UI tasks cover specific route UX problems but not stylesheet ownership/architecture.
